title: Inner MSCHAPv2 authentication failed
plain_english: The TLS tunnel came up fine — the failure is the inner MSCHAPv2 credential check. The server compared the client's password proof against what it has on file for this user, and it didn't match. That means certificates, shared secrets, and policies are all OK; this is about the user's credentials or how the password is stored.

causes.cause: Plain wrong password — or the wrong username variant (user@domain vs DOMAIN\\user vs bare username) resolving to nothing.
causes.next_check: Look at the User-Name in the debug output and test exactly those credentials on the server with radtest or ntlm_auth --username=... --password=...

causes.cause: The backend cannot produce an NT hash: MSCHAPv2 mathematically requires the cleartext password or its NT hash — SSHA/MD5/crypt hashes in LDAP or SQL can never satisfy it.
causes.next_check: Search the debug output for 'No NT-Password' / 'Cleartext-Password' warnings and check how passwords are actually stored in your directory.

causes.cause: The account is locked, expired, or disabled in Active Directory, which surfaces as a generic MSCHAP failure.
causes.next_check: Check the account status in AD and run ntlm_auth manually on the RADIUS host to see the specific NT_STATUS error.
